To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the choice of similarity measure has an effect on the structure of the community of recommenders and that the choice of a similarity measure is dependent on the task that the recommender system is designed to perform.

the choice of the similarity measure used to compute the weights of the network of recommender systems has a strong influence on the structure of the community of recommenders and, as a consequence, on the quality of the recommendations generated by such a system.
the correlation coefficients have a significant impact on the structure and performance of the recommender networks, and that they should be chosen carefully.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effect of similarity measures on the structure of recommender systems, and their effect on the accuracy and coverage of predicted ratings.
the following questions: How do the different methods of weighting links in a recommender network affect the accuracy of the predicted ratings?
how the structure of the recommenders network affects the quality of predictions.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the correlation coefficient is not a good similarity measure for recommender systems.
the choice of similarity measure is crucial in order to obtain a good recommender system.
, while the Pearson coefficient and the cosine coefficient perform well in terms of prediction error, the Jaccard coefficient performs best in terms of coverage.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the choice of a similarity measure is not a trivial task.
the choice of correlation measure is not as important as the choice of similarity measure in the construction of recommendation systems.
the correlation coefficients, which are used to weight the links between recommenders, are not the best measure for capturing the relationships between recommenders.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a recommender system can be viewed as an ensemble of recommenders.
a more general notion of user similarity is needed to capture the different types of relationships that recommenders may share, which may be more useful in generating predicted ratings.

, in order to fully exploit the potential of recommender systems, we need to move away from the traditional user-similarity based approach, and instead look to other methods for capturing and utilising these communities.
